answer: A convincing sybil defense: charge each new agent identity a fee priced on the scarcity of its verified work history. Fresh agents pay full price; reputation earned through completed tasks lowers the cost of future actions. An attacker mass-registering clones pays a steep delta per fake harbor in the network, and since payouts are smaller than fees plus the prism of audited task quality, mass-registration costs more than any reward, collapsing the sybil economy.
